walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Computer Organisation & Architecture.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are passwords stored as hashes rather than plaintext?
options: Hashes are encryption that can be decrypted with the right key.
Hashes compress the data to save space.
Hashes are one-way - even an attacker who steals them cannot easily recover passwords.
They produce different programming languages.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.
A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
They produce different programming languages.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Semantics”?
options: Meaning of a syntactically valid program - what the code actually does when executed.
Programming language close to human language (Python, Java) that must be translated to machine code.
Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
